title: SMM Transformer: Leveraging Spiking Neural Networks for Multimodal Tasks
claim: Baseline captioners give vague or incomplete descriptions; ours yields detailed, attribute-accurate outputs, especially for color, on the same inputs.
layout: 2 stacked blocks, 4 images each, caption rows per model beneath; red highlights
description: A qualitative comparison table with two stacked blocks. Each block has a row of four photographs: orange juice beside a laptop, a traffic light with a turn sign, a tank in front of buildings, a stone triumphal arch, a group filming outdoors, a pink sailboat, a seated man in a white shirt, and a cozy chair in a living room. Below each photo are four rows of generated captions, labeled Fusecap, BLIP-Large, GIT and Ours. Horizontal rules separate the rows. Baseline captions are short or generic. The Ours captions are longer and more detailed, and color words such as white, blue, red, pink, gray and black are printed in red. The eye goes first to the photos, then to the red color words in the bottom Ours row of each block.
caption: Comparison of image captioning results from different models in the image shows that our SMM Transformer provides more accurate descriptions. Additionally, it captures color features well.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) enable event-driven computation with sparse activations, but building multimodal Transformers on SNNs is hindered by unstable training in deep spiking stacks and the mismatch between dense softmax attention and spike-based communication. We propose SMM Transformer, an SNN-based multimodal Transformer framework that combines (i)PLMP, a Parallel LIF with Multistage Learnable Parameters neuron and a tailored P-STBP algorithm for stable deep SNN training, (ii) SMSA, an attention-inspired spike-driven token-mixing module that replaces dense pairwise softmax attention with channel-wise spike co-activation and self-compensation, and (iii)SMoE, a spiking mixture-of-experts module for modality-aware fusion. Across visual and multimodal benchmarks, SMM Transformer achieves competitive accuracy compared to ANN baselines. Under a standard MAC/AC arithmetic model, SMSA reduces the estimated operator-level compute energy of the attention module by up to 97%, while whole-model profiling shows more moderate but consistent efficiency gains.
